coronary artery endothelial dysfunction (CEF) is present in HIV positive individuals (HIV+) without significant coronary artery diseases (CAD).

coronary endothelial dysfunction, a marker of vascular disease and predictor of cardiovascular events, is present in HIV patients with no evidence of CAD, and is as severe in this group as that seen in HIV-negative individuals with CAD.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-positive (Hiv+) individuals with no coronary artery disease (cad) have impaired coronary endothelial function (cef) that is comparable to that seen in hiv− individuals with established cad.
coronary endothelial dysfunction, as measured noninvasibly, is present in HIV patients without significant CAD, is as severe as in patients with known CAD, and is related to inflammation.

The main takeaway from our work is that
HIV patients without known CAD have coronary endothelial dysfunction that is as severe as in CAD patients and is related to the level of systemic inflammation.

HIV-positive patients with no evidence of coronary artery disease have significant coronary endothelial dysfunction and this dysfunction is as severe as the dysfunction seen in HIV-negative patients with known coronary artery disease.
coronary endothelial function is markedly impaired in individuals with HIV who are at low risk of CAD.
